title: Trombone Jones, the drunken Fisk graduate
summary: He tells of a brilliant, perpetually drunk trombonist in the carnival band who had graduated from Fisk and who corrected the college men from under the wagon.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How long did you stay with the carnival?

Oh, let me see, probably, well, we left Florida and came east. We came to Philadelphia. I'm trying to think did we come to New York. Yeah, we came up as far as Philadelphia and Pittsburgh too, I think. We played around the east and then went back to Florida and did Texas and whatnot, you know?
You were with the carnival for quite
I would say a year or two years. I mean yeah, I don't know exactly. I was -- I stayed there, and --
Did you -- were you advancing on your trumpet while you were going with --

Yes. Yes, I was. Because I was the leader, became the leader of the group, and I think we had a pretty good band, and let me think. Who else was there? Oh, that's what I meant to mention. It was a trombone player on this -- Jones, he was on this job. We called him Trombone Jones, and he was a -- he had graduated Fisk University, and he was quite a man. And he -- I remember, and his shoes -- his feet were on the ground. He turned the feet, turned up, and they had ragged clothes on, and he needed a haircut, and he drank. He stayed drunk all the time, as often as he could -- whenever he could find -- get hold of something to drink.

Why I'm mentioning this is because I -- this is how I found out what a man he was, and he'd go lie down under the wagon and go to sleep. So this is -- different guys, you know, who did get a chance to go to school, and you sit down with them. They would pull out those sheepskins. You know.
They must let you know, I went to school too, you know, and my days of college and school and blah, blah, blah, blah, blah. So they're making some point

there, or something, and somebody came in one day and some explanation of something, and he said I know what I'm talking about, so-and-so-and-so-and-so, and this guy, you know, laying under the wagon, he said it was 18 so-and-so-and-so-and-so, and such-and-such, was the case, but so-and-so's theory is much better. Awnkk, went on back to sleep.
And they say who is he? Who's the -- and they stopped. They found out. He say I'm only a graduate of Fisk University.
But he was going down hill at that time.

Oh, yeah, but what a musician! He could play! He was then as good -- well, as the Dorseys now. I use that name because he was widely known. He could send a wire, send a wire to you, or so-and-so-and -- send me a ticket and a hundred dollars, I want to get on your show, and they'd be glad to do it, because they -- the news got around, they said, man, don't send that guy five cents. He'll drink it up. You won't see him. And that was -- you know.
